messages.subject: RE: how to load corpus into Rattle for text mining? [SEC=UNOFFICIAL]
parts:
Hi Paul,
 
I approach textmining with Rattle from a different direction.
 
I start up R studio, and I load text miner, and i set the working directory as my corpus directory. I only have my documents to text mine in there. I then load my corpus and i run my code, to make dictonaries, do frequence counts and assocations, etc. I then create outputs of these files into a variable, which i turn into a dataset, using the code
 
fred <- as.data.frame(Terms(tdm))       
 
you do have add in some variable names to get rattle to load the dataset, as rattle needs a certain number of variables to load, ie greater than just a single variable.
 
Once you have the data loaded into Rattle, you can then graph the frequency counts, terms, and assocations, etc  You cant run a model on the terms, without a Risk and a Target. I have been trying to find a way to do this at the moment,
 
Regards
Tony
 
 
Some example code (theory)
 
library(tm)
library(Rgraphviz)
library(rattle)
rattle()
 
setwd("/home//TmDemo")
 
my.corpus <- Corpus(DirSource("/home//TmDemo"))

my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, stripWhitespace)
my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, tolower)
my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, removeWords, stopwords("english"))
my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, removePunctuation)

my.corpus <- tm_map(my.corpus, stemDocument)
(an example)
tdm1 <- as.data.frame(findAssocs(tdm, "mall", 0.2))

Hi Paul,

There are known issues with Rgraphviz and R. Luckily, its only used in one part of the TM package so far, unfortunately if you want to plot the word connection ploys. which i must say are very good, then you have to have it. There are a range of suggestions on the Internet about getting them both to work, and there are websites which have a download package to help. But I have still not been able to get it to work. Grahams suggestion to me was its easier to get a virtual box running, and then run every thing in a Linux environment, as a fast track while I had a urgent deadline. I was able to access a Linux and print what i needed.

I dont know what the answer is for a pure windows only environment, I have been thinking to explore the SNA package, which has similar graphing capabilities, and seeing if I can just export the data into a social network analysis, or just develop my own plotting sequence in RGL or one of the other plotting packages.

It would be nice if the people who write TM, just wrote that function calling a different package.

However, once you do get the TM package working, it is very easy to provide some impressing results, and as I have said before getting them into rattle is a big advantage.

Regards
Tony
